title: A Night at the Night Market
passage:
On Friday evening, Daniel's family decided to visit the night market near their apartment. The street was crowded with people, and the air was filled with the smell of grilled squid and fried chicken. "I have never seen so many stalls in one place!" Daniel said excitedly to his sister, Amy.

They stopped at a stall that sold bubble tea. The owner, a cheerful man, shouted, "This drink is the most popular one in the whole market!" Daniel decided to try it because he was curious about the taste. Amy chose a cup of mango shaved ice instead, because she thought it looked more refreshing than bubble tea.

As they walked further, they noticed a long line in front of a small shop. "That shop must sell something delicious," their mother guessed. They waited patiently, and soon it was their turn. The stew noodles were too hot to eat right away, so everyone had to wait a few minutes before the noodles were cool enough to eat.

Near the end of the market, Daniel spotted a game stall. He wanted to win a stuffed toy for Amy, so he tried throwing rings at the bottles. Unfortunately, he was not skillful enough, and the rings kept missing. His father, who used to play this game when he was young, offered to help. After several tries, he finally won a small bear for Amy.

Before leaving, they bought a bag of fruit to share at home. "This has been the best night market trip we have had in months," Amy said happily. Daniel agreed that trying new food was always an adventure.

vocab.example: The night market was crowded with people.
They stopped at a stall that sold bubble tea.
The owner of the stall shouted happily.
This drink is the most popular one in the market.
Mango shaved ice tasted more refreshing than bubble tea.
They waited patiently in the long line.
The stew noodles were too hot to eat right away.
He was not skillful enough to win the game.
Unfortunately, the rings kept missing the bottles.
His father offered to help him win the toy.
Trying new food was always an adventure.
Daniel was curious about the taste of bubble tea.
Daniel spotted a game stall near the exit.

grammar: 現在完成時（have/has + 過去分詞）：表示從過去持續到現在的經驗，或強調剛完成的動作。例：I have never seen so many stalls in one place. / This has been the best night market trip we have had in months.
比較級與最高級：比較級用於兩者之間的比較，最高級用於三者以上中最突出的一個。例：The shaved ice looked more refreshing than bubble tea.（比較級）/ This drink is the most popular one in the whole market.（最高級）
too...to / 形容詞 + enough + to：too...to 表示「太...而不能」，enough to 表示「足夠...可以」。例：The noodles were too hot to eat right away. / The noodles were cool enough to eat.

reading.q: Why did Daniel say, "I have never seen so many stalls in one place"?
opts: He had visited this market many times before.
He was surprised by how many stalls were at the market.
He did not like crowded places.
He was looking for his sister.
reading.ex: Daniel 說這句話是因為他從沒看過這麼多攤位聚在一起，表示他對市場的規模感到驚訝。

reading.q: What did Amy choose instead of bubble tea, and why?
opts: Grilled squid, because she was hungry.
Fried chicken, because it smelled good.
Mango shaved ice, because it looked more refreshing.
Stew noodles, because her mother suggested it.
reading.ex: 文中提到 Amy 選了芒果冰，因為她覺得芒果冰看起來比泡泡茶更清涼提神（more refreshing）。

reading.q: Why did everyone have to wait before eating the stew noodles?
opts: The shop had run out of noodles.
The noodles were too hot to eat right away.
The owner was still cooking them.
They were waiting for a table.
reading.ex: 文中說「The stew noodles were too hot to eat right away」，所以大家必須等麵稍微降溫才能吃。

reading.q: Why did Daniel need his father's help at the game stall?
opts: He did not have enough money.
He was not skillful enough at throwing the rings.
He was too tired to continue.
The stall was about to close.
reading.ex: 文中提到 Daniel「was not skillful enough, and the rings kept missing」，所以爸爸主動幫忙。

reading.q: How did Amy describe the night market trip at the end of the story?
opts: A trip she wanted to forget.
The best night market trip they had had in months.
A trip that was too crowded to enjoy.
reading.ex: 文末 Amy 說「This has been the best night market trip we have had in months」，表示她非常滿意這次的夜市之旅。

grammar.q: I have never ___ so many stalls in one place!
grammar.ex: 現在完成時為 have/has + 過去分詞，see 的過去分詞是 seen，故選 C。

grammar.q: This drink is ___ in the whole market.
grammar.ex: 最高級須加 the，且後面常加代名詞 one 代替前面提過的名詞，故選 B。

grammar.q: Amy thought the shaved ice looked ___ than bubble tea.
grammar.ex: 兩者比較要用比較級 more refreshing than，故選 B。

grammar.q: The noodles were ___ hot to eat right away.
grammar.ex: 「too + 形容詞 + to + 動詞」表示「太...而不能...」，故選 too。

grammar.q: The noodles were cool ___ to eat.
grammar.ex: 「形容詞 + enough + to + 動詞」表示「足夠...可以...」，enough 須放在形容詞之後，故選 C。

vocab.ex: crowded 意思是「擁擠的」，形容人多的地方。
stall 指市場或夜市裡的「攤位」。
unfortunately 表示「不幸地」，語意接近 sadly（令人遺憾地）。

vocab.q: The game required him to be ___, but he was not good enough.
vocab.ex: skillful 表示「熟練的」，符合丟圈圈遊戲需要的技巧。
adventure 指「冒險」，文中指嘗試新食物的冒險經歷。
